Proves AR-6's `eq` operator on a `decimal` field (AR-7's typed-value matrix), previously unexercised in this category despite AR-7 requiring `int64`/`decimal`/`double` to be distinguished. AG Grid's number filter has no distinct wire representation for `decimal` vs. `double` (both send a plain JS number, `19.99` here) — the adapter coerces it into a `decimalValue` (`{"type":"decimal","value":"19.99"}`, a numeric *string* per `ir.schema.json`, to avoid float round-tripping loss) using the field's schema-declared `decimal` type (SEM-5), exactly as the boolean-modeling note documents for cases 005/006/044/045. The compiled artifacts carry that string through to Postgres (a text-bound parameter a `numeric` column compares exactly) and to MongoDB (`$numberDecimal` Extended JSON, the same "exact representation over silent precision loss" rationale SEM-4 uses `$date`/plain-string forms for). OpenSearch/Elasticsearch has no arbitrary-precision decimal type in the pinned 7.10-era subset, so the Search artifact represents the value as a plain JSON number identically to a `double` field — a documented, accepted precision-limited divergence (mirroring the Addendum's AGG-5 pattern of naming known backend gaps rather than silently asserting false precision).
